RIFAMPICIN-RESISTANT TB (RR-TB): ROUTINE CARE
Assess the patient with RR-TB At diagnosis, notify1. Also register the patient in the RR-TB register (EDRWeb) once treatment started. Update register at every visit and upon discharge from care.
Assess When to assess Note

Symptoms Every visit • If respiratory rate ≥ 30, breathless at rest or while talking, prominent use of breathing muscles, drowsy/confused, coughs up ≥ 1 tablespoon fresh blood, neck stiffness, persistent vomiting or new weakness of arm/leg, give urgent attention and refer. If persistent episodes of coughing blood, consider referral for surgical review. • Expect gradual improvement. If not improving, assess adherence, other long-term conditions and review DST results. • If still no clinical improvement at 3-4 months or month 3 culture positive, request extended phenotypic DST and present to PCAC/NCAC 200 to advise on rescue regimen.

Adherence Every visit Ask about factors that may influence adherence and give adherence support 195. If returning after loss to follow-up, request extended phenotypic DST on latest positive culture and present to PCAC/NCAC 200 to advise on regimen.

Side effects Every visit • Ask about side effects of treatment 118. Manage promptly as side effects are common cause of treatment interruption. • If intolerance to any medication, present to PCAC/NCAC 200 for medication substitution. • Report adverse events on EDRWeb and to SAHPRA via EDRWeb.

TB contacts At diagnosis • Ask if patient is a TB contact2 of index patient with RR-TB. If yes, check index patient's DST results to help decide patient's RR-TB treatment regimen. • Advise that all TB contacts2 of newly diagnosed RR-TB patient have symptom screen and TB NAAT. If TB NAAT negative, assess for TPT and continue TB symptom screening 3 monthly for first 12 months then 6 monthly up to 24 months. Refer to CHW/WBOTs to do home visit for TB screening/testing or advise self-screening via TB HealthCheck 200.

Family planning Every visit • Check for pregnancy if patient is a woman of child-bearing potential. If not pregnant, advise to avoid pregnancy during treatment and assess patient's contraceptive needs 170. If pregnant, give routine antenatal care 175 and start RR-TB treatment. • If on injectable contraceptive, no need to change interval between doses.
Mental health Every visit If stress, anxiety or low mood, assess and manage further 98.

Alcohol/drug use At diagnosis, if poor adherence In the past year, has patient: drunk ≥ 4 drinks3/session, used illegal drugs or misused prescription or over-the-counter medications? If yes to any 165.

Palliative care If deteriorating If the patient has any of: in bed or chair for 50% or more of the day, dependent on others for most care, has had 2 or more unplanned hospital admissions in past 6 months, unintentional weight loss over the past 3-6 months or the patient/family requests palliative care; chooses to reduce, stop or not have treatment and wishes to focus on quality of life 191.
Weight and BMI4 Every visit If BMI < 18.5, refer for nutritional support. Expect weight gain on treatment and adjust treatment doses. If losing weight on treatment, discuss with specialist/refer.
BP At diagnosis If known hypertension 149. If not, check BP: if ≥ 140/90 148.
HIV At diagnosis and after 3 months of RR-TB treatment if previous test negative

• Test for HIV 124. If positive, give HIV routine care 126. • Avoid giving the following medications together: zidovudine with linezolid; efavirenz with bedaquiline or pretomanid; tenofovir with amikacin.

RR-TB refers to TB that is resistant to rifampicin, with or without resistance to other TB medications. If patient has INH-resistant TB 107. If RR-TB care not available, refer to closest DR-TB treatment initiation site.

1Complete notifiable medical conditions (NMC) case notification form and send to NMCsurveillanceReport@nicd.ac.za or notify electronically: www.nicd.ac.za/nmc-overview/notification-process. 2A TB contact refers to any person who shared an enclosed space (at school, socially, or in a household setting), for ≥ 1 night or for frequent/extended daytime periods, with an adult/adolescent with pulmonary TB ("index patient"), during the 3-month period before the index patient started their TB treatment. 3One drink is 1 tot of spirits, or 1 small glass (125mL) of wine or 1 can/bottle (330mL) of beer. 4BMI = weight (kg) ÷ height (m) ÷ height (m).
